thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: Elevated 5xx and request latency for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in us-east-1. Alert group: api.latency.5xx.region.us-east-1 / triggered at 2026-03-15T03:07:02Z. Potential dependency: AWS STS token calls showing high latency and 500s. Paging kevin-oncall and sre-maria.

sre-maria: acked. I'm looking at the STS graphs now — token latency p95 up from 120ms to 2.8s, error rate ~14%. Correlating with spikes in model init/auth failures for hosted instances.

kevin-oncall: on pager. Repro: curl to our auth proxy -> 503 from upstream STS intermittently. Running quick curl: 
```
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null 'https://sts.amazonaws.com/?Action=GetCallerIdentity&Version=2011-06-15' || true
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\n
```
If STS tokens fail, hosted API gateway returns 502/503 for requests that need fresh creds.

josh-platform: copying metrics from the runtime: hosted token failures correlate with ~30% of new-session requests timing out waiting on credential fetch (kv cache misses). Dedicated pools with short-lived node creds also showing increased auth retries.

emma-support: we already have a few customers reporting increased 5xx and latency via Support. ETA requested for mitigation. We should prepare a brief note for status page + targeted emails for customers with Dedicated capacity.

kevin-oncall: immediate mitigations I'm trying: 1) increase auth proxy retry/backoff to avoid immediate 5xx bubbling up; 2) enable fallback to long-lived credential path for Dedicated pools where allowed; 3) route a portion of traffic to eu-west-1 as a temporary regional fallback for Hosted. Applying patches now.

ops-tim: recommend enabling circuit-breaker at edge for auth failures to fail fast with 429/503 fallback message and avoid head-of-line blocking. Also suggest temporarily raising token TTL on cached prefixes so we hit STS less often.

sre-maria: I'm ssh-ing into auth-proxy autoscaling group to bump client retries and add jitter. Patch command:
```
sudo vi /etc/auth-proxy/config.yml
# set retry: attempts: 5, backoff_ms: 300, jitter: true
systemctl restart auth-proxy
```
Applying in us-east-1 now to 3/4 instances.

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy config update -> staging -> us-east-1 batch-1. CI checks passed.

kevin-oncall: rolling config to 2/4, monitoring error-rate. Setting a small percentage route (5%) for Hosted to eu-west-1 for new requests to test cross-region behaviour.

josh-platform: added temporary reroute config: 
```
routes:
  - name: regional-fallback-us-east-1
    match: region=="us-east-1" && error_rate>0.05
    action: route: eu-west-1
    sample_pct: 5
```
This will not move Dedicated pools — only hosted traffic that can tolerate the latency.

incident-bot: Note: scaling events in dedicated-us-east-1 pool are currently failing due to auth token timeouts. Autoscaler attempts limited to 2 retries.

kevin-oncall: for Dedicated customers where we control keys, switching to customer-provided long-lived creds for node bootstrap where policy allows. Manual step: update node pool config to use managed-credentials: false (will require post-check). Doing one pool now.

emma-support: drafting status page: "Elevated 5xx and latency observed in us-east-1 due to third-party auth token service degradation. We are applying mitigations including retry tuning, temporary regional routing, and credential-path fallbacks. Support will follow up with impacted Dedicated customers." Will paste draft in ~10m.

ops-tim: Observability note: CloudWatch API calls for metrics are also showing elevated latency but not failing entirely — this is making alerting noisy. Temporarily lowered alert sensitivity for non-critical thresholds to reduce noise.

sre-maria: After auth-proxy config change: auth failures dropped to ~6% from 14%. P95 token latency down to 1.1s. Re-run validation: synthetic requests now succeed ~88% (was 62%).

kevin-oncall: good. I'm going to increase reroute sample to 20% for Hosted for next 10 minutes to relieve pressure while STS stabilizes. If eu-west-1 handles it, increase further.

josh-platform: watch: some Dedicated pools still failing scale-ups (policy prevents long-lived creds). Ops note: for affected enterprise customers we need to open a support ticket and offer manual scaling/rollback options.

emma-support: support update posted to channel and internal status draft sent to comms. Will coordinate customer outreach for top 10 impacted accounts.

pagerduty: Handoff: kevin-oncall mentions he needs to hand off to night oncall in 55m. Next oncall: ops-tim. Confirmed. Include runbook snippet in handoff.

kevin-oncall: Handoff notes for ops-tim: 1) monitor auth-proxy errors (metric: auth.proxy.upstream_5xx), 2) if >10% for 15m, increase regional fallback to eu-west-1 for Hosted 50% and notify support, 3) for Dedicated: contact account owners before toggling long-lived creds. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/auth-sts-fallback

ops-tim: ack. I'll take over in 55m. Current plan: keep retry/backoff patch live, maintain 20% regional-sample, and coordinate with support for Dedicated customer exceptions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update: error rate reduced to 4.9% in us-east-1, overall request latency improving. AWS status: STS regional status shows intermittent elevated error rates — monitoring AWS dashboard. If AWS reports resolution, we'll gradually remove fallbacks.

kevin-oncall: closing note: major mitigation actions performed: auth-proxy retry tuning, temporary regional routing for Hosted, selective credential-path fallback for some Dedicated pools, support comms initiated. Moving to monitoring mode and hand off to ops-tim for night shift.

sre-maria: adding retrospective TODOs: add synthetic canaries that use both STS and long-lived paths to detect divergence faster; add per-pool credential-health dashboards; document steps to safely toggle long-lived creds.

emma-support: I'll assemble customer impact list and send to account leads.

ops-tim: taking over. Leaving channel open for follow-up. :eyes:
